subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but detailed TypeScript module for a corporate riot-control armored vehicle, designing it as a 4-wheel truck with a roof water cannon turret, neon light bars, and a matte cyberpunk white/black color scheme.

I'm working out the skeleton structure with chassis root, wheel joints for spinning, and turret yaw/pitch joints, deciding to write custom helpers using the SDK's paint, noise, and glow kit utilities rather than importing catalogs that don't exist as exports. I'm nailing down dimensions (2.4 width, 5.6 length, ~2.3m body height) and working through joint orientations for the wheels, figuring out axle directions and steering hinges for the front pair.

For the body construction, I'm planning to use boxes and frustumBox shapes with sloped surfaces for the hood, applying a panelled paint treatment from the clockwork kit to simulate armor plating with rivets, layered with a grime effect that blends dirt near the bottom using noise and smoothstep for a weathered look.

I also want decals and textures: an invented corp logo ("VANTAGE CIVIC DEFENSE"), hazard stripes, and a "RIOT CONTROL" label, applied via thin plane geometries offset slightly from the hull surface so the SVG text renders cleanly. I'm setting up small helper functions for creating box and cylinder geometries and placing painted parts onto bones at specific positions.

Now I'm working out the vehicle's layout in z-forward coordinates: the lower hull as a wide box roughly 2.3 by 0.7 by 5.4 units sitting around y=0.95, with wheels of radius 0.52 positioned outward at the front and rear corners, and fender covers as flattened boxes layered over the wheel arches to suggest wheel coverage.

I'm also figuring out the upper cab shape, considering a raked windscreen and deciding whether to build it as a rotated box or instead extrude the entire body from a single side-profile silhouette to get a smoother, unified form.

Keeping corners sharp with no smoothing since the profile is already concave but non-self-crossing, which works fine for the hull silhouette. For the windscreen, I'm placing a slanted dark magenta-tinted glass visor as a thin rotated box, computing the slope length and angle to match the hull's incline between the two profile points.

Working out the rotation so the glass tilts backward correctly, then offsetting it slightly outward along the slope's normal so it sits just above the hull surface rather than intersecting it.

Now I'm adding the side windows as thin dark slit boxes with protective vertical wire bars, plus raised door panel details with handles, and planning a logo decal plane on the flank.

I'm placing hazard stripe textures on the rear and under-bumper, a front ram/pusher bar with hazard striping and rubber teeth, dark grille slats with a neon strip, glowing slit headlights, and neon underglow rods along the sill.

For the light bars, I'm doing magenta/cyan cyberpunk halves instead of red/blue, with a roof bar housing, grille light bar, side flank neon strip, and rear bar. On the roof I'm placing a turret ring with a water cannon (yaw/pitch joints, flared nozzle with glowing cyan interior), and I'm figuring out where to fit the water tank cylinder on the rear deck without it sitting too high above the hull profile.

Working through placement, I'm settling on twin cylindrical tanks mounted on either side at the rear with glowing cyan gauge strips, keeping the turret centered between them near the windscreen, and positioning the roof light bar just ahead of the turret.

Checking the cannon barrel's forward reach confirms it clears the light bar comfortably, so I'll tilt the pitch joint slightly upward and move on to building the turret's components -- the base ring, drum, cheeks, and cannon body with a lathed nozzle tip.

Shaping the nozzle profile...

I can repurpose the clockwork texture for the tank's pressure gauge display. For the wheels, I'm designing tires with tread lugs made from small boxes arranged in a ring, plus rims with bolts and a glowing magenta neon ring, and I'm now working out the positioning math so the wheel sits flush against the hull side.

I'm reworking the width proportions so the hull and wheels total roughly 2.9 units, which feels right for an armored vehicle, then adding fender flares to cover the exposed upper portion of each wheel where it pokes outside the hull. Now I'm setting the axle positions front and rear, along with the ground clearance for the hull bottom.

For the underside I'm adding axle rods, differentials, skirt armor panels between the wheels with a neon underglow strip, and a dark undercarriage box. On the roof and rear, I'm planning sirens, antenna whips, a sensor dome, LRAD speaker cones, camera domes, side window cages, and shield hangers with translucent riot shields mounted on the rear flanks, plus rear doors with hazard markings, red glowing taillights, small exhaust details, and a rear bumper step with camera.

Now I'm settling on the color palette — neon magenta, cyan, yellow, and red accents against a body scheme of matte gunmetal-navy with white armored panels, going for a cyberpunk corporate aesthetic with dark lower paint and lighter upper panels.

Writing hull paint shader...

Still designing textures... logo with hexagon and "V" emblem, hazard stripes, riot control text, a glowing LED rear panel with "STAND DOWN" scrolling text, and a translucent cyan shield texture.

I'm also working out the shield shape as an extruded dark part with cyan outline, and designing the windscreen as a textured glass plane with cyan HUD reflection streaks layered over a dark gradient base.

Now I'm positioning the glass plane angled against the sloped front of the hull, sizing pillars and the frame around it, then shaping the nose, hood, and grille geometry at the front of the hull.

Working out the bumper and hazard details: a pusher bar box extending forward with a hazard-striped plane mounted on its front face, adjusting total vehicle length, then placing the headlight slits near the front corners.

Now I'm planning the rear end: a vertical face plane for rear doors with seams, an LED screen panel, vertical glowing red taillight strips near the edges, a hazard strip along the bottom, and twin exhaust stacks rising beside the tanks, plus a rear roof deck profile extending from the back corners.

I'm also fixing up the roof geometry constants, recalculating the windscreen slope center and normal angle, positioning a turret and light bar above the roofline, and figuring out placement for forward-facing LRAD speaker cones mounted near the roof.

Now I'm working out tank dimensions mounted on rear cradles, considering using capsule shapes with rounded end domes for a clean paneled look, and thinking about adding a yellow stripe band around the white tank body.

I'm also sketching a small glowing cyan level-gauge strip on the tank's outer face, then deciding to simplify by placing a single gauge panel on a pump housing box on the rear deck instead of multiple gauges.

With that pump housing placed, I'm sweeping a hose from its top down to the turret base using a catmull curve, attaching it to the chassis bone. Then I'm starting on the skeleton hierarchy -- chassis as root, with wheel and steering joints parented to it, defining hub directions for the steering joints.

Now I'm building the wheel geometry function, constructing the tire as a cylinder and adding tread blocks arranged radially around the axle...

Fine-tuning the cover and neon ring radii so the glowing trim sits just outside the armored hub cover, then moving on to underglow strips beneath the sill and a side neon line along the flank near the stripe placement.

I'm placing glowing side-skirt strips between the wheel arches, sized to avoid overlapping the wheels, then adding fender flares sized to clear the wheel tops and matching drop skirts positioned just outside the wheel's outer edge.

Now I'm adding a mud flap behind the wheel and working through the door seam geometry on the cab's flank, figuring out where the vertical seams should sit relative to the windscreen taper and window strip boundaries.

Then I'm placing the door window glass panel, security bars, handle, hinges, and an armor plate above the window, before moving on to the rear compartment zone for the riot shield mount and logo decal.

I'm sketching the shield's trapezoid outline shape on the side flank facing outward, then working out how to position it relative to the logo decal so the two don't overlap, adjusting their heights on the flank.

I'll drop the flank shield idea and instead place painted shield plates on the rear doors, detail the door panels with window slits, bars, handles, and hinges, plus hazard markings and small logos. For armament detail, I'll skip shields entirely and add a tube launcher bank on the front fenders for tear gas/smoke.

Now I'm planning the rotating beacon with a hinge joint at the roof front corner, antenna whips with spike bases, and the light bar housing with alternating magenta/cyan glow segments and end caps.

I'm also considering a thin header LED strip at the windscreen top edge, a gauge texture import for instrument dials, and setting up a V3 tuple type before writing the actual TypeScript code with bones for chassis-fixed parts.

Defining the color palette and build function...

I'm setting up the chassis joint as the spine bone, then extruding the hull profile along the z-axis with bevels, typing the outline points as coordinate tuples. Now I'm adding an underbelly plate using a box primitive.

Positioning the axles as rods with spheres at the wheel hubs for the driveshaft, then placing the windscreen as an angled plane with its normal vector determining the pillar positions on either side.

Now I'm adding the A-pillars as thin rotated boxes flanking the windscreen, checking they stay within the hull width, then building a roof visor box above the windscreen edge with a glowing accent strip along its front face.

Next I'm working out the hood vent slats as small flat boxes angled slightly to follow the hood's forward slope, calculating the rotation needed so their top surfaces tilt to match the hood's rise toward the back.

Then I'm positioning the front nose grille: a dark backing box on the vertical nose face, with thin glowing cyan slats layered on top to suggest an illuminated grille.

I'm placing a hex-shaped corporate logo plane at the center of the grille, planning to reuse the existing emblem SVG for consistency. For the bumper, I'm building a pusher box mounted below the grille, with a hazard stripe plane, corner caps, and tow hooks, while deciding to skip the push bar rods and ram spikes for now. I'm about to position the fog lights and DRLs symmetrically on either side of the nose.

Now I'm positioning headlight housings at the bumper ends with a cyan glow, planning DRL strips along the nose slope, adding roof rack rails, and shaping a lathed cone profile for the siren speaker housings using a small set of outline points.

Next I'm adding steel spikes as antennas on the rear roof corners using the spike primitive with specific length and radius, then placing a half-dome sensor turret on the roof and figuring out tank positions along the z-axis.

Checking turret radius clearance against the tank cap edges, it fits fine since turret is narrower. I'm placing the turret at z -0.15, with windscreen top at 0.9 and light bar at 0.6, and sizing the barrel to extend to 1.5 so it clears the hood comfortably above roof height. I'm also positioning a pump housing box between the two tanks, centered at z -1.4, y 2.5.

Working out the gauge plane at the rear face of the box, then routing a curved hose path from the pump top up and over to connect at the turret's yaw drum, using a few control points to get a natural arc. For the turret mechanism, I'm defining the yaw joint and pitch joint positions and rotation axes, plus a ring torus and drum cylinder sized to match the joint geometry.

Now I'm building out the cannon assembly: a cylindrical body rod spanning from the trunnion to the muzzle, a breech box, water jacket rings using small torus shapes, and a lathe-profile nozzle at the tip. I'm adding glow discs (cyan, inner and outer) near the muzzle for a cannon-tip effect, plus a top-mounted camera with lens glow and a side sensor, all attached to the pitch bone so they follow barrel rotation.

I'm skipping dual small nozzles and setting the barrel's pitch pose to tilt down about 8 degrees. Now I'm adding flank details — neon strips, logo decal, sill — plus fender-mounted tear gas launchers: three angled tube rods per side tilted forward-up from a mounting block near the front wheel flares, without end caps for simplicity.

For the rear, I'm defining the panel face and door seam geometry, window slit glass with bars, and placing an LED screen plane along with a hazard light strip near the bottom of the rear face.

Now I'm adding glowing red rear light bars, a rear bumper step box, and twin exhaust tips angled under the bumper, then considering placement for a flank logo plane on the side.

I also want a "RIOT CONTROL" plaque on the lower front doors and a unit number plate on the roof, which needs its own facing and up-vector so it reads correctly from the front.

Working through the roof number orientation, I decide it's conflicting with the lightbar and turret placement, so I'll just skip the roof number for simplicity. I still want to add small flank vents behind the door.

Still placing hull details...

The wheel overlap with the hull is minor and will stay hidden. For the rear LED, I'll make an SVG texture with a black background and magenta warning text. I'm sketching a hexagonal logo badge with a stylized "V" emblem using SVG shapes, keeping the total part count and triangle budget manageable.

Realizing white text won't read against a light hull, I'll switch the badge to a dark plaque with a yellow border so "VANTAGE" and "CIVIC DEFENSE" text render clearly in white and cyan. I'm now sketching a similar dark plaque design for the riot control label.

Still writing SVG icon code...

For the hull paint, I'm setting up a procedural shader using the SDK's noise, mix, and smoothstep helpers to blend colors based on surface normal and position, mixing a dirt brown tone into the base material gradient.

Now I'm writing the wheel generation logic, looping over front/rear and left/right positions to create steering and wheel joints with appropriate hinge directions and hub offsets.

I'm deciding against scattering random greeble boxes on the rear deck to keep things simpler, and trimming down the imports to only what's actually used—dropping unused ones like `frame` and `b.cards` while keeping createBuilder, paint, noise, mix, smoothstep, svg, and catmull.

Setting up a decal helper for applying textured planes onto the chassis, then wiring up glow effects for textured elements. Now I'm defining the lightbar segments across the front, splitting them into magenta on the left half and cyan on the right, with matching glowing panels front, rear, and top.
